standard.title: Visual arts across cultures, times and places
standard.description: explore where, why and how visual arts are created and/or presented across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored artworks across cultures and communities and asked questions about artists and their practices (AC9AVA2E01). They can identify similarities and differences across cultural contexts. They have not yet examined how an artist's context (time, place, culture) shapes their approach, or compared artists addressing the same theme from different contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore where, why and how visual arts are created and presented across cultures, times and places, making connections and comparisons between artists and their contexts.

nodes.label: Observing artworks closely
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe an artwork in detail — noticing materials, proportions, patterns and features they didn't see at first — and use questions to develop deeper understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Examine one artwork and share at least two observations — one noticed immediately and one discovered through careful looking.
nodes.typical_width: Examine artworks using close observation strategies; use Viewpoints questions to notice materials, patterns, proportions, colours and features; develop understanding through discussion.
wider: Categorise visual features and cultural works in the school environment (murals, memorials, displays) by purpose — social, decorative, functional, cultural, architectural
Compare how different artists represent the same subject or theme — identify what each emphasises and discuss why

response_modes.reason: Close observation requires technique — students need strategies for discovering what they missed initially (looking through half-shut eyes, considering texture, tracing compositional lines) rather than just looking again.

success_criteria: Shares at least two observations about an artwork — one immediately visible and one discovered through careful looking
Asks at least one question arising from close observation

nodes.label: Artist context and approach
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate an artist's context — when, where and how they work — and explain how context shapes their artistic approach.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one aspect of an artist's context (where they live, when they worked, what influences them) and explain how it connects to one choice in the artwork.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate artists' practices using accounts created or co-created by the artist; use Viewpoints questions about studio, process, materials and engagement with galleries; connect context to specific artistic choices.
wider: Explore artists who work collaboratively — investigate why artists might choose to work as a team; compare a collaborative artwork with a solo work addressing the same theme
Compare how artists from different cultural contexts approach sustainability as a theme — identify how context shapes emphasis, material choices and visual conventions

response_modes.reason: Students who investigate only one artist's context develop limited understanding of how context shapes art. A range of artists — across time, place and culture — shows that the relationship between context and making is consistent but varied.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of artist contexts available (collaborative, cross-cultural, sustainability-focused, time-separated) is genuinely rich — each context type reveals a different dimension of how who you are and where you are shapes what you make.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one aspect of an artist's context
Explains how that context connects to a specific choice in the artwork

nodes.label: Comparing across cultures, times and places
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make connections and comparisons between artists working across cultures, times and places — identifying similarities and differences and explaining how context accounts for them.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare two artworks from different cultures, times or places; identify one similarity and one difference and suggest how context might explain the difference.
nodes.typical_width: Make connections and comparisons across multiple artists and contexts; investigate how the same theme (sustainability, celebration, community) is approached differently; discuss how artworks develop social awareness; explore multiple perspectives on the same event.
wider: Compare artworks addressing sustainability from different cultural contexts — identify how land art, works using recycled materials, and representations of climate effects each reflect their makers' relationships to the environment
Explore artworks by First Nations Australian artists that represent connection to Country/Place — compare with artworks by non-First Nations artists representing the same landscapes

response_modes.reason: Comparative analysis draws on close observation skills and context understanding to produce a higher-order claim: that differences between artworks reflect differences in context, not just differences in style.

success_criteria: Compares artworks from at least two different cultures, times or places
Identifies at least one similarity and one difference, and suggests how context might explain the difference
